study.title: 1 Thessalonians 3 To encourage, perseverance, and holiness in the coming of Christ
study.overview: This chapter shows Paul's pastoral concern with the perseverance of the church in Thessalonica. He explains why he sent Timothy, celebrates the good news received about the faith and love of the brethren, and concludes with a prayer for God to strengthen their hearts in holiness, in the sight of Jesus' return. The text unites pastoral care, realism over afflictions, spiritual joy and eschatological hope.

outline.title: Paul sends Timothy in the midst of distress
outline.explanation: Paul says that he no longer endured uncertainty about the Thessalonians and therefore remained alone in Athens while sending Timothy to strengthen and encourage the church's faith. He recalls that the afflictions were no surprise: they had already been warned that they would suffer opposition, and there was fear that the tempter would have shaken them or made useless the apostolic work.

outline.title: Good news bring comfort and gratitude
outline.explanation: Timothy returns with an encouraging report: the brethren remain firm in faith and love, keep good remembrance of the apostles and desire to review them. This comforts Paul in his own affliction, to the point that he says that now he is still firm in the Lord. Therefore, he intensely thanks God and prays night and day to rediscover them and complete what is lacking in their faith.

outline.title: Prayer for open path, growing love and holiness
outline.explanation: Paul prays that God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ will lead the way to the Thessalonians. Then ask the Lord to increase their love for each other and for all. The ultimate goal is for their hearts to be strengthened, blameless in holiness, in the presence of God, when Christ returns with all his saints.

study.context: The chapter starts from a concrete situation: Paul was in Athens and, prevented from going personally, sent Timothy to know the spiritual condition of the Thessalonians and encourage them. The text itself indicates that this church faced afflictions and that Paul had previously warned them that such sufferings would come. The notes also link the final prayer to the expectation of Christ's coming and the language of a return accompanied by his saints.
study.theology: The chapter teaches that the Christian life includes real afflictions, without this means abandonment of God. Perseverance in faith is a gift that must be strengthened by ministry, encouragement and prayer. Also appears a robust view of God's work: the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ act together in behalf of the church, love grows as a sign of spiritual maturity, and holiness is not an optional detail, but the proper way to wait for Christ's coming. Paul's prayer shows that the pastoral goal is not only emotional consolation, but firm heart, blameless life and preparation for the final encounter with the Lord.

scholarViews.insight: Paul prays that the hearts of the Thessalonians may be strengthened, blameless and holy; the note also notes that at the coming of Jesus he will come accompanied by all his saints, possibly a reference to angels.

Paul's joy in listening to Timothy shows how much the firmness in the faith and perseverance of the converts mattered to the success of the ministry; the note highlights that love is an essential part of a stable faith and an irreproachable life.

The note points out that without love of God and neighbor, there is no true stability in the Christian religion; this love produces firmness and continuity, and therefore is linked to irreprehensibility in holiness in the return of Christ.

questions: What afflictions have threatened your perseverance, and how have you answered them in the light of 1 Thessalonians 3?
How can you encourage the faith of another person in a concrete way, just as Paul sent Timothy?
Is your desire for Christ's return producing more love, holiness and vigilance, or just religious information?
study.practice: This week, choose a person or a small group and do for her what Paul did for the Thessalonians: try to know how faith is, offer specific encouragement, pray for growth in love and holiness, and accompany with a concrete message of care. Also, examine if your hope in the coming of Christ is shaping your daily choices. Reinforce the prayer routine by asking God to strengthen your heart to remain blameless before him.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided allow us to safely affirm that Paul was in Athens, who sent Timothy, that there was concern for afflictions and the perseverance of the church, and that the final prayer aims at the coming of Christ. It is not possible to go further to define with certainty additional historical details, exact chronology, or to identify in a conclusive way to those who refer to the expression "all their saints" beyond the possibilities mentioned by the commentators.
